title: Kodewala Academy – Java Backend Tests: Complete Question Bank (Test 2)

questions.question: Which keyword allows JVM to call the main method?
questions.explanation: `main` must be `public` so the JVM, which is outside the class, can access it.

questions.question: Why is the main method declared static?
questions.explanation: The JVM calls `main` before any object exists, so it must be static and callable via the class name.

questions.question: In Java, file name and public class name:
questions.explanation: A file containing a public class must be named exactly after that class (`Test.java`).

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid Java identifier?
questions.explanation: Identifiers cannot start with a digit, contain hyphens or spaces. Underscores are allowed.

questions.question: Java identifiers are:
questions.explanation: `name` and `Name` are different identifiers.

questions.question: What is the default value of a boolean variable?
questions.explanation: Instance/static boolean fields default to `false`.

questions.question: Which variable is declared inside a method?
questions.explanation: Variables declared inside a method/block are local variables.

questions.question: Which variable belongs to an object?
questions.explanation: Each object has its own copy of instance variables.

questions.question: There is only one copy of a ______ variable for the entire class.
questions.explanation: Static variables belong to the class and are shared by all objects.

questions.question: Which operator is used for assignment?
questions.explanation: `=` assigns a value; `==` compares.

questions.question: Which operator returns true only when both conditions are true?
questions.explanation: Logical AND (`&&`) is true only if both operands are true.

questions.question: Which of the following is a benefit of methods?
questions.explanation: Methods let you write logic once and reuse it, improving readability.
`true || false` is `true`.

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-primitive data type?
questions.explanation: `String` is a class (reference type). The others are primitives.

questions.question: Which access modifier allows access only within the same class?
questions.explanation: `private` members are visible only inside their own class.

questions.question: What is the purpose of command-line arguments?
questions.correct_answer: B. Pass dynamic input at runtime
questions.explanation: They let you pass values to `main(String[] args)` when launching the program.

questions.question: What will happen if the public class name and file name are different?
questions.explanation: `javac` rejects a public class whose name does not match the file name.
10 > 5 and 10 < 20 are both true.

questions.question: Which memory optimization issue can occur if instance variables are used where static variables should be used?
questions.explanation: Every object gets its own copy of an instance variable, wasting memory for data that could be shared.

questions.question: Which statement about local variables is TRUE?
questions.correct_answer: C. Must be initialized before use
questions.explanation: Local variables get no default value; the compiler requires initialization before use.
Three arguments (A, B, C) are passed, so `args.length` is 3.

questions.question: Which of the following can be accessed without creating an object?
questions.explanation: Static members are accessed through the class name.

questions.question: Which statement regarding protected members is correct?

options.D: Accessible in same package and subclasses

questions.correct_answer: D. Accessible in same package and subclasses
questions.explanation: `protected` = package access plus access from subclasses (even in other packages).
`a || b` is true, and `!true` is false.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid method name according to conventions?
questions.explanation: Methods use camelCase starting lowercase. A leading capital is the convention for class names.

questions.question: Which scenario is best suited for a static variable?

options.D: Company Name Shared by All Employees

questions.correct_answer: D. Company Name Shared by All Employees
questions.explanation: Static fits data common to all objects; the others are per-object.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Access Modifiers in Java?

options.B: To control the visibility and accessibility of classes, methods, and variables
options.D: To convert source code into bytecode

questions.correct_answer: B. To control the visibility and accessibility of classes, methods, and variables
questions.explanation: Access modifiers (public, protected, default, private) enforce encapsulation.

questions.question: A banking application has a variable balance. The company policy states that balance should not be modified directly by any class outside BankAccount. Which access modifier should be used for the balance variable?
questions.explanation: `private` restricts access to the declaring class; expose it via getters/setters.

questions.question: An e-commerce application has these requirements: every product has its own price; all products share the same GST_RATE = 18%. Which design is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Price is per object (instance); GST rate is common to all (static).

questions.question: An application stores employee IDs. The expected number of employees may grow to several million in the future. Which data type is the safer choice?
questions.explanation: `byte` (±127) and `short` (±32,767) overflow; `int` handles about 2.1 billion.

questions.question: A file-processing application needs the file path to be supplied at runtime because it changes between environments (Dev, QA, Prod). What is the best approach?

options.B: Store it in a local variable
options.C: Take it as a command-line argument

questions.correct_answer: C. Take it as a command-line argument
questions.explanation: Command-line arguments let you supply environment-specific values without changing code.

questions.question: A banking application performs this validation: `if(balance > 0 && accountActive)`. If balance > 0 is false, what happens?
questions.explanation: `&&` short-circuits: if the left side is false, the right side is not evaluated.

questions.question: Which Eclipse shortcut is used to execute the current line of code and move to the next line during debugging?
questions.explanation: F6 = Step Over.

questions.question: During debugging in Eclipse, you are stopped at a method call and want to enter inside that method to debug its code. Which shortcut should you use?
questions.explanation: F5 = Step Into.

questions.question: During debugging in Eclipse, you want to continue program execution until the next breakpoint is encountered. Which shortcut should you use?
questions.explanation: F8 = Resume.

questions.question: While debugging in Eclipse, you have stepped into a method and now want to return to the calling method. Which shortcut should you use?
questions.explanation: F7 = Step Return (finish the current method and return to the caller).
The quiz key marks Compilation Error as correct. By real Java behaviour the output would be option A (`0` then `null`) (int fields default to 0, references to null).

options.A: Default constructor will be automatically created
options.B: Object will be created with id = 0

questions.explanation: Once any constructor is declared, the compiler no longer supplies the default one, so `new Employee()` has no matching constructor.

questions.question: Which is the superclass of all classes in Java?
questions.explanation: `java.lang.Object` is the root of the class hierarchy.
In a different package, default `x` is inaccessible and `protected y` is not accessible via a plain object (Main is not a subclass), so compilation fails. Only `z` (public) is accessible.
